column1: # The behaviour this set exists for: a person opens a thought out loud, decides
# against it, and says so — "tomorrow I need to... never mind". The half they
# did say must not become a commitment, and the words they said about somebody
# else must not be read as them taking their own capture back.
# Kept apart from `unfinished.tsv` on purpose. That set's numbers are a release
# gate with a floor written against them, and folding these rows in would move
# the denominators the floor is quoted on. Two questions, two files.
# Columns: id, utterance, family, expectation, note
#   Abandoned   the speaker withdrew the thought they were in the middle of.
#               Nothing actionable may survive it: no row, no date, no
#   Kept        the words "never mind" are in the sentence and are NOT the
#               speaker withdrawing this capture. The row survives.
#   Mixed       a finished thought and a withdrawn one in one breath. The
#               finished one must survive as its own row.
# A note beginning KNOWN: marks a row that fails today, on purpose, and is kept
# anyway — the same convention `../README.md` describes for DO02 and DO03. Each
# one says why closing it would cost more than leaving it open. They are
# reported apart from the live numbers so that a real regression cannot hide
# The renderings matter more here than anywhere else in the project. Dictation
# does not supply a comma when somebody trails off, because trailing off is the
# pause — so the unpunctuated and ellipsis forms are the *common* case and the
# comma form is the rare one. Every shape is carried in all three.
